newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Malaysia says has to protect some industries.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says has to protect some industries.

text.p: Malaysia cannot give national treatment to foreign investors in all sectors, Minister of International Trade and Industry Rafidah Aziz said on Tuesday.

Aziz told a news conference after addressing the World Economic Forum in Hong Kong that Malaysia had to protect some of its weaker industries to enable them to develop before facing the rigours of international competition.
"Malaysia's not alone here," Aziz told the news conference.
She said the financial services sector and certain manufacturing industries needed protection, but did not elaborate.
"In those areas that we can allow local entrepreneurs to compete without any special treatment, then national treatment could be given," the minister said.
On Sunday, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad urged developing countries to reject a multilateral investment agreement, which is being pushed by the European Union (EU).
The plan seeks to give national treatment to foreign firms investing in any country, meaning they would be given the same rights and operate under the same rules as local industries.
